chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Abi Usamah or someone else, who said:
One time I climbed Mount Abi Qubays while the people were performing the maghrib prayer, and I saw that the sun had not set; it had only become hidden behind the mountain from the people.
Then I met Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام and informed him of that, so he said to me: “Why did you do that? Evil is what you did.

You only perform it when you no longer see it. If it disappears or goes down behind a mountain—so long as clouds or darkness are not covering it and casting shade over it—then what concerns you is only your own east and west, and it is not upon the people to investigate.”

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib prayer and its time at sunset
key_terms.جَبَلٍ: a mountain that blocks direct sight of the sun
key_terms.ظُلَمٌ: darkness or gloom that conceals visibility
key_terms.مَشْرِقُكَ: your local east; your own observational horizon
key_terms.مَغْرِبُكَ: your local west; your own observational horizon

ai.seo_question: When does the time of maghrib prayer begin if the sun is hidden behind a mountain?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the time of maghrib prayer based on ordinary visible sunset from the observer’s own horizon. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام reproves burdening oneself with elevated observation and explains that people are not required to investigate beyond their normal line of sight.
